newsitem.title: PANAMA: Former Panamanian henchman extradited from Peru.
newsitem.headline: Former Panamanian henchman extradited from Peru.

text.p: A henchman of Panama's jailed former strongman Manuel Antonio Noriega was extradited from Peru on Thursday to serve a 20-year prison sentence for killing an army major who tried to topple Noriega in 1989, police said.

Heraclides Sucre, a major in the now defunct Panama Defence Forces, was sentenced in absentia in 1994 for killing Moises Giroldi, who plotted a coup against Noriega, two months before the December 1989 U.S. invasion that ousted him.

Sucre received political asylum in the Peruvian Embassy in Panama during the government of former President Alan Garcia, who was a critic of the United States' invasion. He lost asylum in 1990 under the administration of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori and was arrested last June in Lima for not having proper immigration papers.
Noriega, serving a 40-year prison sentence in Florida on drug and racketeering charges, was also sentenced to 20 years for Giroldi's killing.
In a separate trial, Noriega was sentenced on lesser charges for ordering the killings of at least nine soldiers involved in the attempted coup who had seized him at gunpoint.

When expected U.S. military support failed to materialise, the soldiers released Noriega, who promised them amnesty. Instead Noriega had them rounded up, taken to Albrook Field, a former U.S. Air Force base, and ordered them shot. The incident is known as the Albrook massacre.
